invariants.rationale: Since object.toString() is returning a String and per Java spec, every object's toString() returns a non-null String.
The method directly returns object.toString(), so the result must equal the output of that call.
Calling object.toString() without a null check means object must not be null at this point.
Because result equals object.toString(), their String lengths must also match.
The method's return type is String, so result must be of class String.
